pull-based-delivery-and-the-repository-a.r: A manual change in the cluster fixed an urgent bug and was forgotten, then disappeared at the next deploy and the bug returned. With the repository as the source of truth, the change had to be committed, so it persisted.
pull-based-delivery-and-the-repository-a.x: Pull-based delivery removes cluster credentials from CI and makes drift visible. It also moves complexity into the repository structure, so decide how you handle secrets, promotion and emergencies.

installing-argo-cd-and-the-application-r.r: A team installed the tool with default admin access and shared the initial password. They later set up single sign-on and project-level permissions so each team could manage only its own applications.
installing-argo-cd-and-the-application-r.x: The delivery tool has broad access to your clusters, so secure it like production: SSO, least privilege, upgrades and backups of its configuration.

sync-health-and-drift.r: An application showed OutOfSync because a controller mutated a field after deploy. Ignoring that field in the comparison removed the noise, and real drift stayed visible.
sync-health-and-drift.x: Sync status and health answer different questions. Choose manual or automated sync per environment, understand pruning and self-heal, and make sure alerts exist for Degraded states.

helm-and-kustomize-with-argo-cd.r: A chart was rendered differently in the pipeline and in the cluster because of version mismatches. Pinning the tool versions and rendering the same way in both places made previews reliable.
helm-and-kustomize-with-argo-cd.x: Know exactly how manifests are produced and keep that identical in review and in the cluster. Prefer small overlays and values, and avoid hidden transformations.

environments-app-of-apps-and-application.r: Creating an application per cluster by hand took days and drifted over time. An ApplicationSet generated them from a list, so adding a cluster was a one-line change.
environments-app-of-apps-and-application.x: Generators multiply both convenience and blast radius. Limit what a template can create, protect the repository paths and preview changes before they fan out.

hooks-sync-waves-and-progressive-deliver.r: A database migration needed to finish before the new version started. A pre-sync hook and ordered waves ran the migration first, and the rollout waited for it.
hooks-sync-waves-and-progressive-deliver.x: Ordering is a smell if overused. Make changes backward compatible where possible, keep hooks idempotent and consider progressive delivery with automated analysis for risky rollouts.

access-projects-secrets-and-multi-cluste.r: A team could deploy to the wrong cluster because projects were not restricted. Limiting allowed destinations and repositories per project closed the gap.
access-projects-secrets-and-multi-cluste.x: Projects are the authorisation boundary. Keep secrets out of the repository with an external mechanism, limit cluster credentials and plan how you handle a lost or compromised management cluster.

debugging-argo-cd.r: An application was stuck OutOfSync. The diff showed a field that a mutating webhook changed every time, which explained the loop. Adding an ignore rule for it fixed the noise.
debugging-argo-cd.x: Read the diff, events and controller logs in that order. Separate repository, rendering, cluster and permissions problems, and avoid forcing syncs that would hide the real cause.
